title: Turn Ideas Into Decks
description: A cleaner, more strategic version of the Codex-to-PowerPoint workflow: use AI to structure the deck while keeping judgment, taste, and accuracy human.
alt: Infographic showing a four-step roadmap for turning ideas into decks: objective, inputs, story, and polish, with a reminder that strategy and final judgment stay human.
thesis: Codex can organize the work. You keep the strategy.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: A better deck begins with the decision.

steps.title: Objective
steps.body: Name audience, decision, and outcome.

steps.title: Inputs
steps.body: Gather notes, data, and constraints.

steps.title: Story
steps.body: Build the narrative before slide design.

steps.title: Polish
steps.body: Review accuracy, flow, tone, and readiness.

starter: Ask for a slide-by-slide narrative outline.

title: The Brief Before The Prompt
description: A strategy-first guide for marketers: clarify the decision, audience tension, promise, proof, and tradeoff before asking AI for ideas.
alt: Watercolor infographic showing a vague prompt cloud becoming a clear strategy compass, with five briefing inputs to define before prompting AI: decision, audience tension, promise, proof, and tradeoff.
thesis: Bad AI output is usually a briefing problem.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: AI gets more useful when the assignment is judgeable.

steps.title: Decision
steps.body: What choice should the work influence?

steps.title: Audience tension
steps.body: Whose need, fear, or objection matters now?

steps.title: Promise
steps.body: What belief should the work strengthen?

steps.title: Proof
steps.body: What evidence makes the claim credible?

steps.title: Tradeoff
steps.body: What are we choosing not to say or do?

starter: Before prompting, write the decision in one sentence.

title: Pressure-Test The Strategy
description: A campaign pressure test for finding weak assumptions, thin proof, exclusion risk, and unclear measurement before production starts.
alt: Infographic showing a two-by-two pressure-test matrix for campaign strategy: assumption, proof, exclusion, and measurement.
thesis: Find the fragile assumption before production makes it expensive.

steps.title: Assumption
steps.body: What must be true for this to work?

steps.title: Proof
steps.body: What evidence supports the main claim?

steps.title: Exclusion
steps.body: Who could this confuse or leave out?

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: What signal changes the next decision?

starter: Ask where this strategy is most fragile.

title: Evidence-Led AI Research
description: A disciplined research loop for using AI to structure inquiry without turning uncertainty into false confidence.
alt: Infographic showing an evidence ladder: question, sources, tensions, implications, with a guardrail to keep evidence and interpretation separate.
thesis: Use AI to structure inquiry, not invent certainty.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: Strong synthesis shows what is still unknown.

steps.title: Question
steps.body: Write the decision the research supports.

steps.title: Sources
steps.body: Map credibility, recency, and perspective.

steps.title: Tensions
steps.body: Compare disagreement instead of smoothing it.

steps.title: Implications
steps.body: Turn evidence into choices and risks.

title: Draft Before Automating
description: A trustworthy implementation map for moving from source material to draft output, human approval, and automation only after the workflow earns trust.
alt: Infographic showing a workflow map: source, draft, approve, automate, with privacy boundary and human review gates.
thesis: Automation should follow trust, not excitement.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: The safest workflow keeps drafts out of live systems.

steps.title: Source
steps.body: Define which records count as truth.

steps.title: Draft
steps.body: Generate in a private review space.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: Require a clear human yes.

steps.title: Automate
steps.body: Scale only after repeated trust.

starter: Add a review gate before publishing.

title: Accessible Content Is Better Marketing
description: A disability-aware content QA model that treats access, dignity, readability, and choice as part of marketing quality.
alt: Infographic showing a four-part accessible content checklist: plain, scannable, respectful, and reviewed.
thesis: Access is content quality, not final polish.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: Good marketing respects attention and energy.

steps.title: Plain
steps.body: Remove jargon and buried actions.

steps.title: Scannable
steps.body: Use headings, lists, and clear labels.

steps.title: Respectful
steps.body: Avoid pity, blame, or deficit framing.

steps.title: Reviewed
steps.body: Let disabled users shape assumptions.

starter: Check the message for cognitive load.

title: Advocacy Prep, Not Replacement
description: A careful parent/supporter workflow for organizing facts and questions without asking AI to make legal, school, or care decisions.
alt: Infographic showing advocacy prep steps: privacy, facts, questions, follow-up, with a guardrail that AI prepares but does not replace advocacy.
thesis: AI can prepare advocacy work. It should not replace advocacy.

steps.title: Privacy
steps.body: Remove identifying school and health details.

steps.title: Facts
steps.body: Separate events from interpretations.

steps.title: Questions
steps.body: Name what needs clarification.

steps.title: Follow-Up
steps.body: Track commitments, owners, and dates.

starter: Turn notes into facts and questions.

title: The Privacy-First Support Brief
description: A least-sensitive context brief for families who need to coordinate support without overexposing a child's life.
alt: Infographic showing a privacy-first support brief with sections for context, needs, questions, and commitments.
thesis: Share enough to help, not everything you know.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: The least-sensitive version is often enough.

steps.title: Context
steps.body: Say what matters for this meeting.

steps.title: Needs
steps.body: Group support needs without overexposure.

steps.title: Questions
steps.body: List what others must answer.

steps.title: Commitments
steps.body: Track who owns the next step.

title: Listening For The Child's Signals
description: A dignity-first way to use AI for organizing observations around environment, communication, sensory load, recovery, and what helped.
alt: Infographic showing a signal map for organizing observations around environment, communication, sensory load, recovery, and what helped.
thesis: Use AI around the child's signals, not over them.

shift.label: Useful shift
shift.note: The goal is support, not control.

steps.title: Privacy
steps.body: Remove names, faces, dates, and places.

steps.title: Context
steps.body: Note environment, demands, and timing.

steps.title: Signals
steps.body: Describe communication without blame.

steps.title: Helped
steps.body: Document support, recovery, and preferences.

title: Lower-Demand Transitions By Design
description: A practical model for changing the environment, reducing friction, offering choices, and preserving agency during transitions.
alt: Infographic showing a pathway for lower-demand transitions: moment, friction, choices, recovery.
thesis: Change the environment before blaming the child.

steps.title: Moment
steps.body: Name the change that may feel hard.

steps.title: Friction
steps.body: Look for sensory, timing, or demand load.

steps.title: Choices
steps.body: Offer acceptable options with agency.

steps.title: Recovery
steps.body: Plan time and space afterward.

starter: Ask how to lower the demand.

title: What AI Should Never Decide
description: A signature boundary-setting guide for knowing which decisions belong with people, lived experience, and qualified professionals.
alt: Infographic showing a boundary board for decisions AI should never make: diagnosis, rights, safety, discipline, placement, consent, and identity.
thesis: Responsible AI means knowing what deserves protection.

steps.title: Rights
steps.body: Do not outsource legal or school decisions.

steps.title: Care
steps.body: Do not diagnose or prescribe support.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: Do not delegate crisis judgment.

steps.title: Identity
steps.body: Do not interpret lived experience for someone.
